security_audit.summary: No evidence of prompt injection or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files. The static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, placeholder API key examples, Data Commons client method names, and public documentation links.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment-variable examples and warn users not to paste real Data Commons API keys into prompts or shared notebooks.
State that custom Data Commons endpoints should be trusted before use because queries are sent to that service.

content.value_statement: Public statistical data can be hard to identify, query, and compare across places. This skill guides Data Commons API usage for observations, entities, and DCID resolution.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation and authentication for datacommons-client with Pandas support.
Shows observation queries for population, income, unemployment, health, and environmental data.
Explains name, coordinate, and Wikidata ID resolution into Data Commons IDs.
Documents node queries for properties, names, relationships, and place hierarchies.
Describes conversion of observation responses into dictionaries and Pandas DataFrames.
Covers data availability checks, facet filtering, and relation expressions.
limitations: Requires the external datacommons-client package and a Data Commons API key for the default service.
Data accuracy, availability, and freshness depend on Data Commons source datasets.
Does not include executable helper scripts or a local data cache.
Custom Data Commons endpoints must be chosen and trusted by the user.

use_cases.title: Compare Regional Indicators
use_cases.description: Compare population, unemployment, or income measures across states, counties, or countries using Data Commons observations.

use_cases.title: Resolve Place Identifiers
use_cases.description: Convert names, coordinates, or Wikidata IDs into DCIDs before building repeatable queries.

use_cases.title: Explore Public Data Graphs
use_cases.description: Inspect entity properties, names, and place hierarchies to understand available public datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Population Statistic
prompt_templates.prompt: Use datacommons-client to find the latest population for California. Explain the DCID and statistical variable choices before querying.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Places
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare median household income for California counties in 2020. Include the relation expression and table fields I should review.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Ambiguous Names
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve Springfield as a city, explain ambiguity handling, then show how to choose the correct DCID before querying population.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reproducible Analysis Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Data Commons workflow for multiple cities, with name resolution, data availability checks, facet filtering, and Pandas-ready outputs.

output_examples.input: Latest population for California and Texas
output_examples.output: A short explanation of selected DCIDs and Count_Person, followed by a table-ready result summary.

output_examples.input: Find counties inside California and compare income
output_examples.output: A workflow using a contained-in-place relation, county names, income variable guidance, and sorted comparison output.
A resolved place identifier, available variable guidance, and suggested observation queries for local analysis.

best_practices: Resolve names to DCIDs before querying observations.
Check data availability before choosing statistical variables.
Filter facets when consistent sources matter.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into prompts or shared files.
Do not assume a variable exists for every place or date.
Do not use custom endpoints unless the source is trusted.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The default datacommons.org service requires a Data Commons API key.

faq.question: Can it work with Pandas?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation shows Pandas support and DataFrame-ready observation outputs.

faq.question: What kinds of data can it query?
faq.answer: It covers demographic, economic, health, environmental, and other public statistical datasets available in Data Commons.

faq.question: Can it resolve place names?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides name, coordinate, and Wikidata ID resolution into Data Commons IDs.

faq.question: Does it include executable scripts?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and examples for using the Python client.

faq.question: Can I use a custom Data Commons endpoint?
faq.answer: Yes. Use only trusted endpoints because queries and configuration may be sent there.
